newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Illness and injury have hit the West Indian cricket camp putting Brian Lara and Curtly Ambrose off the team's list for an indefinite time, however, it is hoped Lara will play in the final lead-up match against the Australian XI. Page 22.

Australian selectors have moved Tim Horan from the wing to inside centre and named David Campese in a shadow Test team to play Ulster in Belfast on Sunday. The game may be Campese's last chance to play for Australia before he retires. Page 22.

Catriona Matthew leads the field in the A$350,000 Alpine Australian Ladies' Masters being held at Royal Pines. Matthew has a score of 65 and is only one shot ahead of New South Wales' Joanne Mills. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Bowler Glenn McGrath limped out of today's Sheffield Shield match against Queensland with a heel injury, only 24 hours after fellow Australian bowler Damien Fleming broke down with a thigh muscle strain. Page 44.

The wind has become a decisive factor in the Australian PGA yesterday after three hours of play was cancelled when winds swept up to speeds of 50 knots. Several players will return in the morning to complete their first rounds. Page 44.
The Wallabies have won their game against Connacht, 37 to 20, in Ireland, before a crowd of almost 3,500. George Gregan was the top scorer for Australia with two tries. Page 43.
THE AGE

Fast bowler Glenn McGrath is the latest casualty in the growing list of Australian cricketers out with injuries. McGrath returned home with a heel injury and withdrew from the Sheffield Shield match against Queensland today. Page C8.

The MCG may be the venue for the pre-season Ansett Cup grand final next March. The AFL yesterday released this and other details of its 1997 night competition draw, which will begin on 21 February. Page C8.

Play at the Australian PGA Championships was halted yesterday as winds gusted up to 48 knots and made play impossible. Wayne Riley and Bryan Roach of New South Wales currently hold the lead on 66, two shots ahead of the next pack. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

Before the big winds attacked the A$400,000 Australian Open yesterday, Wayne Riley and unknown Bryan Roach managed to post 66. Wayne Smith shares the lead at six under par and will hit off again this morning. Page 112.

Saintly's trainers and owners are playing down the horse's cold which it has had since arriving in Tokyo on Tuesday for the racing of the Japan Cup. Trainer Bart Cummings said that early detection and treatment will allow Saintly to race in top form for he Cup. Page 112.

Victoria's 22-year-old Craig Lowndes is one step closer to racing at Formula One level after yesterday completing 30 laps in his first Formula 3000 race. Formula 3000 is the stepping stone for racing drivers to get into Formula One. Page 110.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Cathy Freeman has made her first competitive appearance in Australia since competing in the Atlanta Olympics. Freeman finished second, clocking only 11.99 seconds in the 100 metres - 0.75 seconds off her best time. Page 110.

The Australian Rugby Union yesterday announced that Sydney could have hosted the Bledisloe Cup at a cost of A$500,000. Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett strongly denies that money changed hands to get the event to Melbourne. Page 110.

Following Saintly's 20-hour trip into Tokyo the Melbourne Cup winner has suffered a cold. The cold is a minor setback for the four-year-old in its build up to the Japan Cup and Bart Cummings said he is not overly concerned, as the cold is being treated. Page 110.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
